column4: Summary
column5: Description

column4: Programme setup and governance
column5: Jira and Azure DevOps setup, open questions from section 18, risks, hiring, stakeholder sign-offs, and phase exit gates.

column4: Azure landing zone and network
column5: Hub-and-spoke network in UK South and UK West: Azure Firewall, ExpressRoute, Bastion, Private DNS, Front Door + WAF, Application Gateway, and APIM networking.

column4: CI/CD and DevOps platform
column5: Azure DevOps pipelines for infrastructure, cluster add-ons, application images, GitOps promotion, Databricks bundles, and model releases.

column4: Operational data stores
column5: Azure Managed Redis, Cosmos DB, Azure SQL, and Event Hubs for the decision path.

column4: Data platform and lakehouse
column5: ADLS Gen2, Delta Lake Bronze/Silver/Gold, Data Factory, Databricks, Unity Catalog, Purview, tokenisation, and data quality (FR-9).

column4: Feature Store and online features
column5: Feature groups from section 6, point-in-time training sets, and sync to Redis and Cosmos DB.

column4: Decision core
column5: Decision, rules, and scoring services: p99 under 200 ms, 2,000 TPS sustained and 5,000 at peak, with fallback rules (FR-1, FR-2, FR-3).

column4: Case management and investigator portal
column5: Alerts, cases, SLAs, and the Angular portal screens (FR-4, FR-5, FR-6).

column4: Case Copilot
column5: Grounded, cited case summaries through Microsoft Foundry, with no decision authority (FR-7).

column4: Strategy and rules tooling
column5: Rule authoring, backtests, threshold simulation, and two-person approval (FR-8).

column4: Models and MLOps
column5: fs-txn, fs-anomaly, and fs-mule models; MLflow and Unity Catalog registry; promotion gates; monitoring and retraining (FR-10).

column4: Security and compliance
column5: PCI DSS scope, PRA and FCA operational resilience, UK GDPR, PSR APP-scam reimbursement, key management, segregation of duties, and penetration tests.

column4: Testing and quality
column5: Test strategy, environment and data testing, functional and UAT, performance, and contract tests (section 14).

column4: Observability and operations
column5: Logs, metrics, traces, alerts, dashboards, ServiceNow, and runbooks.

column4: Resilience and multi-region
column5: Active-active decisions in two regions, failover under 5 minutes with no accepted decisions lost, and Chaos Studio tests.

column4: Shadow run, rollout, and go-live
column5: Full-volume shadow run, go-live criteria, and phased rollout one channel at a time (phases 5 and 6).

column4: Create the FS Jira project, import this backlog, and set up the board
column5:
Create the FraudShield (FS) Jira project, import jira-import.csv, create sprints 1 to 6, and set up the Scrum board with swimlanes per epic.

Acceptance criteria:
* All epics and issues imported with parent links
* Sprints 1 to 6 exist with the dates in BACKLOG.md
* All five team members can see and update the board

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Request the Azure DevOps project, repository, and Azure subscriptions
column5:
Raise the requests for the FraudShield Azure DevOps project and Git repository, and for subscriptions (or management groups) for dev, test, perf, and prod. Nothing else in Azure can start until these exist.

Acceptance criteria:
* Azure DevOps project and repo exist and the code is pushed
* Subscription IDs recorded for each environment
* Anoop has Owner rights to run the bootstrap

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Confirm the client and payment rails in scope (open question 1)
column5:
FraudShield now deploys to UK South and UK West, so section 18's assumption of an Australian bank becomes a UK bank with card, Faster Payments, and online transfers. The sponsor must confirm this, because it drives channel integration, mTLS certificates, and the rollout order.

Acceptance criteria:
* Sponsor decision recorded in Confluence or the ticket
* In-scope rails listed with their channel owners
* Design assumptions updated if different

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Assess available labelled history: 24 months of transactions and outcomes (open question 2)
column5:
Section 18 assumes at least 24 months of transactions and outcomes. Section 16 rates poor or delayed labels as a high risk owned by Anoop. Find the sources for analyst outcomes, chargebacks, and scam claims, and estimate their coverage and lag.

Acceptance criteria:
* Sources, volumes, and date ranges documented
* Label lag measured for chargebacks (up to 90 days) and claims
* Go or no-go recommendation for Phase 3 modelling

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Confirm device and behaviour signals supplied by the banking app (open question 3)
column5:
The device and session feature group depends on signals sent with each request: device age, remote-access signal, and new location. The channels lead must confirm what is available.

Acceptance criteria:
* List of available signals with field names
* Gaps raised as risks
* Decision API request contract updated

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Confirm the regulations and contracts that apply (open question 4)
column5:
The design was written for Australian regulation. For the UK deployment, compliance must confirm which obligations apply (PCI DSS; PRA SS1/21 and FCA SYSC 15A operational resilience; UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018; the PSR APP-scam reimbursement rules; and the Money Laundering Regulations 2017 for AML escalation) and re-baseline design section 12.

Acceptance criteria:
* Applicable obligations listed by Compliance
* Owner named for each obligation
* Security epic E12 updated

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Agree whether tokenised case data may be sent to the language model (open question 5)
column5:
The design assumes only tokenised case data is sent, to a UK deployment. Security and Privacy must decide before the Copilot pilot.

Acceptance criteria:
* Security and Privacy decision recorded
* Data allowed in prompts listed
* Region and data residency confirmed

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Build the Phase 1 Azure cost model (open question 6)
column5:
Estimate monthly run cost per environment from the Terraform SKUs: AKS node pools, APIM, Front Door Premium, Azure Firewall, ExpressRoute, Managed Redis, Cosmos DB multi-region, SQL, Event Hubs, Databricks, and Foundry. Code: infra/terraform/env/*.tfvars

Acceptance criteria:
* Cost per environment, with prod in two regions
* Main cost drivers and savings options listed
* Presented to the sponsor

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Coordinate hiring for the roles the team is missing
column5:
Section 15 needs 2 ML engineers, 3 to 4 senior Java engineers, 1 to 2 Angular developers, 2 DevOps or SRE engineers, 1 security engineer, and part-time fraud strategist and model risk owner. Section 16 says hire before Phase 2 or use a specialist partner.

Acceptance criteria:
* Hiring plan with dates for each role
* Partner option assessed for low-latency Java
* Status reported in each sprint review

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Set up the RAID log with the risks from section 16
column5:
Record every risk from section 16 with impact, response, and owner, and review it at each sprint review.

Acceptance criteria:
* All eight design risks recorded with owners
* Review cadence agreed
* New risks from Sprint 1 added

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Agree the segregation-of-duties roster
column5:
Rule authors, model authors, and approvers must be different people (section 12). Agree who holds each role so pipeline approvals and the strategy service can enforce it.

Acceptance criteria:
* Roster agreed by fraud, risk, and security leads
* Approver groups created in Entra ID
* Azure DevOps environment approvers match the roster

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Phase 1 exit gate: security and data approval
column5:
Phase 1 (Foundation) exits when security and data owners approve the landing zone, CI/CD, and labelled history.

Acceptance criteria:
* Evidence pack prepared: Terraform plans, network diagram, test results, label assessment
* Security and data owners sign off
* Phase 2 start confirmed

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Set up sprint ceremonies and the stakeholder cadence
column5:
Plan sprint planning, reviews, and retros, and a fortnightly update for fraud, risk, and security leaders.

Acceptance criteria:
* Calendar invites sent
* Stakeholder list with contact owners
* First sprint review booked

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Get stakeholder agreement on the proposed non-functional targets
column5:
Section 1 says all targets are proposed until confirmed in Phase 1: p99 under 200 ms, 2,000 TPS sustained and 5,000 peak, 99.99% availability, failover under 5 minutes, 75% recall at 0.2% alert rate, and 7-year replay.

Acceptance criteria:
* Each target confirmed or changed by its owner
* Changes reflected in test plans
* Decision recorded

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Coordinate vendor accounts: Microsoft, Databricks, and the ExpressRoute provider
column5:
Set up account contacts, support plans, and quota requests (AKS cores, Cosmos DB regions, Foundry model quota in UK South).

Acceptance criteria:
* Named contacts for each vendor
* Quota requests raised
* Support plan level confirmed

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Phase 2 readiness check: hires and partner in place
column5:
The design says the decision path must not be built without senior low-latency Java experience. Confirm people are in place before Phase 2 work starts.

Acceptance criteria:
* Java and DevOps roles filled or partner contracted
* Onboarding plan ready
* Open role tickets reassigned

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Design the IP address plan for hub, app spoke, and data spoke in both regions
column5:
Allocate non-overlapping ranges for hub, decision and application spoke, and data and ML spoke, for dev, test, perf, and prod in UK South and UK West, leaving room for on-premises ranges over ExpressRoute. Code: infra/terraform/env/*.tfvars

Acceptance criteria:
* Address plan agreed with the bank network team
* No overlap with on-premises ranges
* tfvars updated

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Review and apply the hub-network module to dev
column5:
Hub VNet with Azure Firewall, Bastion, and Private DNS zones. Code: infra/terraform/modules/hub-network

Acceptance criteria:
* Plan reviewed and applied through infra.yml
* Bastion reaches a test VM in each spoke
* Firewall policy in place with deny by default

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Review and apply the app-spoke and data-spoke modules with hub peering
column5:
Decision and application spoke (AKS, APIM, private endpoints) and data and ML spoke (Databricks VNet-injected, Data Factory runtime). Code: infra/terraform/modules/app-spoke, infra/terraform/modules/data-spoke

Acceptance criteria:
* Both spokes peered to the hub
* Subnets sized for AKS, APIM, Databricks host and container, and private endpoints
* No public IPs outside the edge

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Link Private DNS zones for all private endpoints
column5:
Zones for Redis, Cosmos DB, SQL, Event Hubs, ADLS, Key Vault, ACR, Foundry, and Databricks, linked to hub and spokes.

Acceptance criteria:
* Every private endpoint resolves to a private IP from both spokes
* No public resolution from inside the VNet
* Zones managed by Terraform

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Route spoke egress through Azure Firewall
column5:
User-defined routes send spoke egress to the firewall. Allow only the FQDNs AKS, Databricks, and the pipelines need.

Acceptance criteria:
* AKS nodes pull images and reach Azure APIs through the firewall
* Denied traffic is logged
* Allow-list documented

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Validate Databricks VNet-injection subnet sizing
column5:
Check that host and container subnets support peak cluster sizes for streaming and training jobs.

Acceptance criteria:
* Maximum node count per subnet calculated
* Subnet sizes confirmed or changed
* Decision recorded

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Order ExpressRoute circuits for both regions
column5:
Coordinate with the provider and the bank network team for circuits to UK South and UK West.

Acceptance criteria:
* Provider selected and order placed
* Lead time recorded as a risk if it threatens Phase 2
* Peering details shared with Sri Gowthami

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Design ExpressRoute connectivity to the payment switch and core banking
column5:
Design private peering, gateways in the hub, route filters, and resilient paths for both regions.

Acceptance criteria:
* Design reviewed with the bank network team
* Failover path between regions documented
* Terraform change ready for when circuits arrive

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Apply the edge module: Front Door Premium and WAF for the portal
column5:
Front Door Premium with WAF (DRS 2.1, bot rules, UK-only geo rule) in front of one Application Gateway per region. Application Gateway accepts traffic only from the AzureFrontDoor.Backend service tag, and Front Door checks the origin certificate. The module is created only when origin_certificate_secret_id is set. Code: infra/terraform/modules/edge

Acceptance criteria:
* Portal path reachable only through Front Door
* WAF in prevention mode in test
* Origin not reachable directly from the internet

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Configure Application Gateway and APIM in internal mode
column5:
APIM runs in internal VNet mode in the app spoke; Application Gateway publishes the portal and admin APIs. Code: infra/terraform/modules/apim, infra/terraform/modules/edge

Acceptance criteria:
* APIM gateway reachable only privately
* Health probes green
* Same-region private path for channels (20 ms budget)

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Set up mTLS for payment channels at API Management
column5:
Validate channel client certificates at APIM, and design certificate issue and rotation with the channel teams.

Acceptance criteria:
* Requests without a valid client certificate are rejected
* Certificate rotation runbook
* Tested with a stub channel

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Set up Private Link connectivity from the payment switch
column5:
Design the private link path from the payment switch to API Management shown in Figure 5.

Acceptance criteria:
* Design agreed with the switch owner
* Connection tested in test
* Signed requests from the switch documented

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Apply the landing zone to the test environment
column5:
Promote hub and spokes to test through infra.yml using env/test.tfvars.

Acceptance criteria:
* Test plan reviewed and applied
* Connectivity checks pass
* Differences from dev documented

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Baseline NSGs and VNet flow logs across spokes
column5:
Apply NSGs to every subnet and send flow logs to Log Analytics.

Acceptance criteria:
* Every subnet has an NSG
* Flow logs visible in Log Analytics
* Traffic analytics enabled

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Assign Azure Policy guardrails for the landing zone
column5:
Allowed regions (UK South and UK West), required tags, deny public network access on data services, and require private endpoints.

Acceptance criteria:
* Policies assigned at subscription scope
* Existing resources compliant
* Exemptions documented

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Create the fraudshield-api and fraudshield-portal app registrations and app roles
column5:
fraudshield-api: Application ID URI api://<client ID>, scope access_as_user, accessTokenAcceptedVersion 2, and app roles ANALYST, TEAM_LEAD, STRATEGIST, RISK_APPROVER, ML_ENGINEER, MODEL_RISK_OWNER, CHANNEL, and DECISION_ENGINE. Assign DECISION_ENGINE to the decision service's managed identity, and CHANNEL to the API Management identity. fraudshield-portal: single-page application granted access_as_user. Set ENTRA_API_CLIENT_ID and ENTRA_SPA_CLIENT_ID for Terraform. Code: services/common/.../security/Roles.java

Acceptance criteria:
* Both registrations exist with the eight app roles
* Role groups mapped to the segregation-of-duties roster
* Portal sign-in works in dev

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Grant Azure SQL access to the case and strategy identities
column5:
Run CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER and grant db_datareader, db_datawriter, and db_ddladmin (for Flyway) to id-fraudshield-<env>-case and id-fraudshield-<env>-strategy, as the SQL admin group. Code: services/case and services/strategy migrations

Acceptance criteria:
* Both services start against Azure SQL
* No SQL logins or passwords exist
* Access reviewed by security

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Deploy the first-release services and portal to dev
column5:
Build decision, case, strategy, copilot, and portal with app.yml and release them to dev. Check readiness: the decision service stays not-ready until it has loaded rules from strategy. Code: services, portal, deploy/gitops

Acceptance criteria:
* All five apps Synced and Healthy in Argo CD
* A test payment through API Management reaches the alert queue
* Portal screens load with Entra sign-in

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Test the portal screens against the design mock-ups with Playwright
column5:
End-to-end tests for the six screens in design section 9: overview, alert queue, case investigation, rules and thresholds, model monitoring, and release approval, including keyboard-only use (WCAG 2.2 AA). Code: portal

Acceptance criteria:
* One test per screen runs in CI against dev
* Reason-required and self-approval rules covered
* Accessibility checks pass

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Replace in-memory velocity and profile stores with Managed Redis and Cosmos DB
column5:
The first release keeps counters and profiles in memory per pod. Move velocity counters to Azure Managed Redis (atomic, geo-replicated) and profiles to Cosmos DB, keeping the 25 ms timeout and safe defaults. Code: services/decision/.../features

Owner: Java Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Counters are shared by every pod and both regions
* p99 feature retrieval under 30 ms at 5,000 TPS
* Timeouts fall back to defaults and flag reduced confidence

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Replace the in-memory event queue with the Cosmos DB outbox and Event Hubs
column5:
Decisions, alerts, and counts are queued in memory in the first release, so a pod restart can lose them. Write each decision to the Cosmos DB outbox in-line and publish to Event Hubs afterwards; move idempotency keys to the same store. Code: services/decision/.../events

Owner: Java Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* No accepted decision is lost when a pod or region fails
* Idempotency holds across pods
* Lakehouse receives every decision

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Build the ONNX scorer with signed-model loading
column5:
Scoring mode 'model' refuses to start in the first release, which uses the labelled fs-baseline-1 score instead. Load fs-txn from immutable storage, verify its signature, and run it with ONNX Runtime in-process. Code: services/decision/.../scoring

Owner: Java Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Inference p99 under 15 ms
* An unsigned or altered model is refused
* Shadow version scored with no effect on decisions

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Push live alert and SLA updates to the portal with Azure SignalR
column5:
The first-release portal refreshes the queue and overview every 30 seconds. Push new alerts and SLA changes through Azure SignalR Service. Code: portal

Owner: Angular Developer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* New alerts appear within 2 seconds
* Falls back to polling if SignalR is unavailable
* No customer data in SignalR messages

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Connect rule backtests to Databricks SQL
column5:
The Backtest button returns 'not set up' in the first release. Run rule backtests against 30 days of history through the Databricks SQL API, and refresh score_distribution daily for the threshold simulator. Code: services/strategy

Owner: Java Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Backtest result shown within 2 minutes
* Simulator data refreshed daily
* Queries run as a service principal

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Write release approvals to the Unity Catalog approval tag
column5:
Approvals are recorded in the strategy service. The release pipeline reads approval.approved_by from Unity Catalog, so sync each approval there, and post gate evidence from the validation jobs to /api/v1/models/{model}/releases. Code: services/strategy/.../models

Owner: ML Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Approval in the portal sets the tag
* Gate evidence arrives without manual steps
* model-release.yml passes the approval gate

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Set up the releases branch and build service permissions
column5:
Pipelines write release state to the releases branch: image tags (app.yml), model versions (model-release.yml), and Terraform outputs (infra.yml). Give the project Build Service identity Contribute and Create branch on the repository, deny Contribute on releases to everyone else, and keep releases out of the CI trigger. Code: azure-pipelines/scripts/commit-release.sh

Acceptance criteria:
* Build service can push to releases
* People cannot push to releases
* Every change on releases links to the pipeline run that made it

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Create the fraudshield-private agent pool inside the network
column5:
Production Databricks has no public access, so the prod stage of databricks.yml and the gate checks in model-release.yml run on an agent pool named fraudshield-private. Create a Managed DevOps Pool (or scale-set agents) in the primary data spoke, with private DNS resolution and egress through the firewall.

Acceptance criteria:
* Pool named fraudshield-private is online
* Agents resolve and reach the private Databricks workspace
* No public inbound access to the agents

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Issue the portal origin certificate and enable the edge
column5:
Issue a certificate for the origin host name, import it into the environment Key Vault, and set ORIGIN_HOST_NAME and ORIGIN_CERTIFICATE_SECRET_ID in the variable group. Then add an APIM policy that accepts portal calls only with the X-Azure-FDID header equal to the front_door_id Terraform output.

Acceptance criteria:
* Certificate in Key Vault with a renewal owner
* Edge module applied and portal_url works
* Portal API calls without the Front Door ID are rejected

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Record AKS_CLUSTERS and GITOPS_REPO_TOKEN in each environment variable group
column5:
After the first apply, infra.yml prints the AKS_CLUSTERS value. Add it, and a read-only repository token for Argo CD as the secret GITOPS_REPO_TOKEN, to fraudshield-<env>. Rotate the token every 90 days until Argo CD uses workload identity for the repository.

Acceptance criteria:
* Both values set for dev and test
* Token is read-only and stored as a secret
* Rotation reminder created

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Run the bootstrap script: Terraform state storage and geo-replicated registry
column5:
Run infra/bootstrap.sh once in the shared subscription. It creates the state storage account and a Premium ACR replicated to UK West.

Acceptance criteria:
* State storage has no public blob access
* ACR geo-replication to UK West
* Output values stored in the fraudshield-shared variable group

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Create the fraudshield-azure service connection with workload identity federation
column5:
Federated service connection with no stored secrets, and the role assignments the README lists.

Acceptance criteria:
* Service connection verified
* Roles scoped to FraudShield subscriptions
* No client secret exists

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Create variable groups and environments with approvals
column5:
Variable groups fraudshield-shared and fraudshield-<env>; environments fraudshield-dev, -test, -perf, -prod. Prod approvers come from the segregation-of-duties roster.

Acceptance criteria:
* All groups and environments exist
* Prod requires a named approver who is not the change author
* Pipelines limited to main for apply

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Make ci.yml a required check on main
column5:
Pull request validation: terraform fmt and validate, Trivy IaC and Kubernetes scans, helm lint and kubeconform for every service in every environment, shellcheck, and service tests. The Databricks bundle is validated by databricks.yml, because validation needs the workspace. Code: azure-pipelines/ci.yml

Acceptance criteria:
* Branch policy requires ci.yml to pass
* Minimum one reviewer
* Pipeline green on main

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Add branch policy, PR template, and CODEOWNERS
column5:
CODEOWNERS routes network changes to Sri Gowthami, data changes to Priyanka, and pipeline changes to Anoop.

Acceptance criteria:
* CODEOWNERS file merged
* PR template asks for test evidence
* Reviewers added automatically

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: First run of infra.yml to dev, and fix what the first plan finds
column5:
Plan, approval, and apply for dev. Expect provider, quota, and naming issues on the first run. Code: azure-pipelines/infra.yml

Acceptance criteria:
* Dev plan reviewed and applied
* Second plan shows no changes
* Fixes merged through pull requests

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Install cluster add-ons on dev AKS with platform.yml
column5:
Argo CD, Argo Rollouts, internal ingress-nginx, and Prometheus (for canary analysis) installed with az aks command invoke, because the cluster API is private. Third-party images are imported into the shared registry first, because AKS egress allows only the registry and Microsoft endpoints. KEDA, workload identity, and the Key Vault CSI driver are AKS add-ons set by Terraform. Code: azure-pipelines/platform.yml, azure-pipelines/scripts/install-platform.sh, deploy/platform

Acceptance criteria:
* All add-ons healthy
* Argo CD reachable only privately
* Re-running the pipeline makes no changes

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Apply the Argo CD AppProject and ApplicationSet
column5:
One ApplicationSet per cluster creates an application per service. Configuration comes from main (deploy/gitops), and release state (image tag, model version, Terraform outputs) from the releases branch. Code: deploy/gitops/argocd

Acceptance criteria:
* ApplicationSet creates apps from the environment folder
* AppProject restricts namespaces and repos
* Sync status visible

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Deploy the Databricks Asset Bundle to dev
column5:
Run azure-pipelines/databricks.yml for the dev target. Code: databricks/databricks.yml

Acceptance criteria:
* Bundle validates and deploys
* Jobs owned by a service principal, not a person
* Run as a pipeline, never from a laptop

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Prove app.yml end to end with a placeholder service
column5:
Build one image, scan it with Trivy, write the tag to environments/dev/release.yaml on the releases branch, and wait for the Argo rollout to be healthy. Every service in the ApplicationSet needs an image, so start with placeholder images for services that have no code yet. Code: azure-pipelines/app.yml, deploy/helm/fraudshield-service

Acceptance criteria:
* Image built once and promoted by its commit-SHA tag
* Canary steps 5%, 25%, 100% observed
* Rollout aborts when the analysis fails

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Promote infrastructure and the placeholder service to test
column5:
Run infra.yml and app.yml for test.

Acceptance criteria:
* Test applied with no manual steps
* Same image digest as dev
* Smoke tests pass

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Define pipeline quality gates
column5:
Agree which results fail a build: unit tests, Trivy critical and high findings, SonarQube quality gate, and kubeconform errors.

Acceptance criteria:
* Gate thresholds documented
* Gates enforced in ci.yml and app.yml
* Exception process agreed

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Add SonarQube or GitHub Advanced Security to ci.yml
column5:
Section 13 names GitHub Advanced Security or SonarQube. Choose one and add it to pull request validation.

Acceptance criteria:
* Tool chosen and recorded
* Scan runs on every pull request
* Quality gate blocks merges

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column4: Write post-deployment smoke tests
column5:
Smoke tests run after each environment deployment: health endpoints, APIM route, and private endpoint reachability. Code: azure-pipelines/scripts

Acceptance criteria:
* Smoke stage fails the pipeline on error
* Results published to the run
* Runs in dev and test

Source: FraudShield Solution Design Document, Draft 1.0.

column5:
